questions.q: How did the house in Saville Row look the day after Fogg came home?
choices: Its doors and windows were still closed
Every lamp in the house was lit for a party
Its door was hung with a sign saying For Sale
A crowd of reporters was waiting on the steps
questions.evidence: His doors and windows were still closed

questions.q: The chapter says Fogg laid wagers "for honour's sake." What does this suggest about why he made the bet?
choices: He badly needed the money to pay his debts
He cared more about honour than about getting rich
He wanted to become famous in the newspapers
He wished to prove the Reform Club members wrong about India
questions.evidence: laid wagers for honour's sake than for the stake proposed

questions.q: What did Passepartout do first when he got back to the house?
choices: Put out the gas burner that had burned for eighty days
Lit a fire in his master's room to warm the house
Wrote a letter of apology to the Reform Club
Opened all the windows wide to let in the cold fresh winter air
questions.evidence: had extinguished the gas burner, which had been burning for eighty days

questions.q: How did Passepartout spend the first night back in London?
choices: Sleeping soundly after the long journey
Keeping watch all night at his master's door
Walking the streets looking for Fix
Packing his bags to leave Mr. Fogg's service
questions.evidence: Passepartout watched all night, like a faithful dog, at his master's door.

questions.q: When Passepartout asked his master why he did not curse him, what did Mr. Fogg say?
choices: "I blame no one."
"It was your fault."
"Fix is to blame."
"Leave my house now."

questions.q: What did Mr. Fogg not do on Sunday for the first time since he had lived in the house?
choices: Eat his breakfast of tea and a chop
Set out for his club at half-past eleven
Wind the great clock in the front hall
Read the morning newspapers by the fire
questions.evidence: did not set out for his club when Westminster clock struck half-past eleven

questions.q: Passepartout "looked ruefully at the young woman." What does ruefully mean?
choices: Angrily
Sadly and with regret
With great surprise and joy
Cheerfully
questions.evidence: looked ruefully at the young woman

questions.q: What did Mr. Fogg first ask Aouda when he sat down with her that evening?
choices: Whether she would pardon him for bringing her to England
Whether she wished to go back home to India
Whether she knew where Fix had gone after Liverpool
Whether she could lend him money to pay his debt to the club
questions.evidence: will you pardon me for bringing you to England?

questions.q: What did Mr. Fogg offer Aouda now that he was ruined?
choices: A ticket on a steamer back to Bombay
The little he had left
A place in his friend's house
A letter to her relatives
questions.evidence: I beg to place the little I have left at your service.

questions.q: What did Aouda ask Mr. Fogg after he said he had no friends or relatives?
choices: If he would take her to see the Reform Club
If he would have her for his wife
If he would let her find work in London
If he would forgive Passepartout at last
questions.evidence: Will you have me for your wife?

questions.q: What is the most important thing that happens in this chapter?
choices: Fogg and Aouda tell each other their feelings and plan to marry
Fogg sells his house in Saville Row to pay what he owes the Reform Club
Passepartout finds Fix and makes him apologise to Fogg
Aouda decides to return to India with Passepartout
